  obtain ⟨theta, _, hlimit⟩ := exists_twoEdgeDominant_nonreal_phase Q hQ
  have hscaled :=
    tendsto_realExp_re_mul_twoEdgeExponentialMode_logMesh hwre hwim theta P Q
  have himscaled : Tendsto (fun k ↦
      ((Real.exp (twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseTranslation w.im theta k * w.re) : ℂ) *
        twoEdgeExponentialMode w P Q
          (twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseTranslation w.im theta k)).im)
      atTop (nhds (Complex.exp (-((theta : ℂ) * I)) * Q).im) := by
    simpa [Function.comp_def] using
      (Complex.continuous_im.tendsto _).comp hscaled
  have heventNonzero : ∀ᶠ k in atTop,
      ((Real.exp (twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseTranslation w.im theta k * w.re) : ℂ) *
        twoEdgeExponentialMode w P Q
          (twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseTranslation w.im theta k)).im ≠ 0 :=
    himscaled.eventually_ne hlimit
  have hindex := tendsto_twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseIndex_atTop hwim theta
  intro N
  have heventIndex : ∀ᶠ k in atTop, N ≤ twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseIndex w.im theta k :=
    hindex.eventually_ge_atTop N
  obtain ⟨k, hkIndex, hkNonzero⟩ :=
    (heventIndex.and heventNonzero).exists
  refine ⟨twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseIndex w.im theta k, hkIndex, ?_⟩
  rw [← twoEdgeLogMeshPhaseTranslation]
  intro hzero
  apply hkNonzero
  rw [Complex.mul_im]
  simp only [Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, hzero, mul_zero, zero_mul,
    add_zero]

charge to vanish. If not, extract exact positive obstruction and replacement selection law.

## Frozen conjecture

For a finite matrix `M` and any unitary Schur triangularization `Uᴴ M U=T`, define

`Q(T)=Σ_i 100(Im T_ii)²(6(Re T_ii)²+23(Im T_ii)²)`.

Then:

1. `Q(T)=0` iff every zero of `det(1-zM)` is real.
2. If `det(1-zM)=0` for some nonreal `z`, then `Q(T)>0` for every Schur triangularization.
3. At every theta approximation accuracy `k`, there exists an admissible source stage `SK` with a
   nonreal divisor such that every Schur packet of `blockMatrix SK.2 SK.1` has strictly positive
   quartic charge.

Therefore current `ThetaSourceSignedApproximationProperty` cannot imply quartic-charge vanishing.
Any surviving GTA construction must add a selection rule that excludes positive charge inside each
approximation fibre.

## Hostile attacks

- Zero Schur diagonal entries: they generate no finite determinant zero and have zero charge.
- Repeated eigenvalues and arbitrary Schur ordering.
- Non-normal matrices: use triangular determinant product only.
- Nonreal determinant variable is reciprocal to a nonzero Schur diagonal node; check imaginary-part
  inversion in both directions.
- No claim that fixed `Classical.choice` stage is bad; theorem concerns specification fibre.

## Dependency-closed proof

Fix Schur data `U,T` for `M`. Packet faithfulness gives `Q(T)=0` iff every `T_ii` is real.
Schur triangularity gives

`det(1-zM)=Π_i(1-zT_ii)`.

If every `T_ii` is real and the product vanishes, one factor vanishes. That diagonal entry is
nonzero, and taking imaginary parts of `1-zT_ii=0` forces `Im z=0`.

Conversely, suppose every determinant zero is real. For each nonzero `T_ii`, the reciprocal
`z=T_ii⁻¹` zeros the corresponding factor and hence the determinant. Therefore `Im(T_ii⁻¹)=0`.
The identity `Im(w⁻¹)=-Im(w)/normSq(w)` and `normSq(T_ii)≠0` force `Im T_ii=0`.
Zero diagonal entries are already real. This proves the generic iff.

If a nonreal determinant zero exists, generic iff forbids zero charge. Nonnegativity then makes
charge strictly positive, for every Schur packet. Existing source-specific nonselection supplies,
at each accuracy `k`, an admissible `SK` and nonreal `z` with
`det(1-z blockMatrix(SK))=0`. Applying the generic strict theorem to an arbitrary Schur packet of
that block matrix proves positive charge throughout the bad-stage Schur fibre.

# The analytic-to-real theta-defect comparison has exactly the off-real divisor as kernel

- **ID:** `theta-analytic-to-real-defect-kernel-is-offreal-divisor`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper); terminal Route-A reduction
- **Scientific status:** `[BRIDGE; NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE]`
- **Source:** the theta analytic cokernel and the Xi logarithmic-derivative real-boundary measure
- **Statement:** On the algebraic semisimplification of the Xi analytic defect, the canonical map to
  the positive real-boundary defect is projection onto the real zero fibers.  Its kernel is exactly
  the sum of the nonreal zero fibers.  Hence faithfulness of this comparison is equivalent to RH.

## Analytic semisimple defect

Let `Z_Xi` be the distinct complex zero set of

```text
XiC(z)=xi(1/2+i z).
```

The semisimplification of the analytic cokernel of multiplication by `XiC` has algebraic
finite-support core

```text
D_an^alg=direct_sum_(rho in Z_Xi) C e_rho.              (1)
```

The logarithmic-derivative boundary theorem constructs the real defect core

```text
D_real^alg
  =direct_sum_(gamma in Z_Xi intersect R) C e_gamma,    (2)
```

with positive weights equal to the analytic multiplicities.

## Canonical comparison

The comparison from analytic support to the real boundary is restriction to the real spectral
axis:

```text
r(e_rho)=e_rho if rho is real,
r(e_rho)=0     if rho is nonreal.                       (3)
```

Therefore

```text
ker r
  =direct_sum_(rho in Z_Xi, Im(rho)!=0) C e_rho,        (4)

range r=D_real^alg.                                    (5)
```

Both identities follow immediately on the basis and remain valid for any completion on which the
coordinate maps are faithful.

## RH equivalence

By (4), `r` is injective exactly when every Xi zero is real.  Under

```text
s=1/2+i rho,
```

reality of `rho` is exactly `Re(s)=1/2`.  Hence

```text
r is faithful on the analytic semisimple defect
  iff RiemannHypothesis.                                (6)
```

This theorem does not prove injectivity.  It proves that the proposed real-boundary exhaustion is
the RH statement itself after the source and target defects have been constructed.

## Consequence

The positive real-boundary measure is a genuine source object, and the analytic theta cokernel is a
genuine source-first divisor object.  Their comparison supplies no intermediate localization law:
its missing injectivity is exactly the absence of off-line zeros.

Any successful pro-geometric continuation must therefore introduce additional pre-divisor prime
geometry that proves injectivity.  Rephrasing (3) as a faithful functor or purity axiom is circular.

# Transported prolate relative-resolvent corner

- **ID:** transported-prolate-relative-resolvent-corner
- **Stage:** 3-formalized / needs independent audit
- **Type:** THEOREM / CONTROL MODEL (paper)
- **Scientific status:** BRIDGE / NOT NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE
- **Sources:** Connes--Moscovici, *Prolate spheroidal operator and Zeta*, arXiv:2112.05500;
  Connes--Consani--Moscovici, *Zeta zeros and prolate wave operators*, arXiv:2310.18423v2;
  Ramis--Richard-Jung--Thomann, *New eigenfunctions for the negative part of the
  Connes--Moscovici prolate spectrum*, 2025

## Statement

Fix a cutoff `lambda>0` and a prime `p`, and put `P={p}`. Let `W_(lambda,infinity)` be the unique
archimedean self-adjoint prolate extension commuting with the physical and Fourier cutoffs. Let

`theta_P:H_infinity->H_P`

be the source bounded isomorphism carrying the archimedean Sonin space onto the semilocal Sonin space.
Define the transported closed prolate control

`W_(lambda,P)^theta=theta_P W_(lambda,infinity) theta_P^(-1)`. (1)

Then:

1. `W_(lambda,P)^theta` is closed, similar to a self-adjoint operator, and its resolvent is trace
   class at every nonreal `z`;
2. the semilocal Sonin space reduces its resolvent;
3. for the cyclic transition `eta_P`, the exact relative-resolvent Sonin corner

   `C_(P,lambda)(z)
    =(1-Q_(lambda,P))
      ((W_(lambda,P)^theta-z)^(-1)eta_P
       -eta_P(W_(lambda,infinity)-z)^(-1))
      Q_(lambda,infinity)`                                  (2)

   is trace class and nonzero for every nonreal `z`.

Thus prolate resolvent smoothing really does convert the noncompact Euler metric crossing into a
nonzero trace-class exact-Sonin corner, uniformly at the level of existence for every positive cutoff.

## Archimedean spectral input

Connes--Moscovici prove that `W_(lambda,infinity)` is the unique self-adjoint extension commuting with
both cutoffs, that its spectrum is discrete and unbounded in both directions, and that every negative
eigenfunction belongs to the Sonin space. The Sonin restriction has at most finitely many positive
exceptions; the orthogonal complement carries the classical positive prolate spectrum and its Fourier
replica.

Ramis--Richard-Jung--Thomann construct spectral determinants for the classical and nonclassical
spectra which are entire of order at most `1/2`. The exponent of convergence of their zeros is therefore
at most `1/2`; in particular the reciprocal eigenvalue sequence is summable. Together with the finite
multiplicities, this gives

`(W_(lambda,infinity)-z)^(-1) in Schatten_1`                (3)

for every nonreal `z`.

Similarity by the boundedly invertible `theta_P` preserves closedness and the trace-class ideal, proving
items 1--2.

## Relative-corner proof

The source relation between the cyclic and Sonin transitions is

`eta_P=theta_PG_P`,

where `G_P` is the positive inverse Euler metric/cyclic-density multiplier. Pulling (2) back through
`theta_P` and applying `sonin-relative-resolvent-sylvester-factorization.md` gives, up to a bounded
invertible quotient map,

`R_complement(z)H_P-H_PR_Sonin(z)`,                         (4)

where

`H_P=(1-Q_(lambda,infinity))G_PQ_(lambda,infinity)`.

The inverse Euler corner `H_P` is noncompact for every `lambda>0`, hence nonzero. Both restricted
resolvents in (4) are trace class by (3), so (4), and therefore (2), is trace class.

/-
# Verified-height amplification from equivariant zero censuses

This module isolates the exact integer input that can extend a verified RH height without any
minimum-modulus computation.  `RHVerifiedThrough H` records that every positive-ordinate strip zero
through height `H` is on the critical line.  `stripZeroIncrement H U` is the finite set of strip
zeros in the half-open increment `(H, U]`.

The capstone `rhVerifiedThrough_amplify_of_increment_ncard_le_one` says that a census of at most one
new distinct zero amplifies RH from `H` through `U`.  The reason is quantized and uniform at the
critical line: an off-line zero and its critical-line reflection are two distinct members of the
increment.  Unlike a modulus or logarithmic-derivative margin, this count does not decay when the
off-line pair approaches the line.

The theorems are bridges, not the missing analytic estimate.  The second capstone weakens a census
of the whole increment to an equivariant collar: at most one zero near the critical line and no
zeros in one outer wing.  Reflection supplies the other wing.  This is the right interface when
the verified endpoint itself may be a simple critical-line zero, so a full top-edge nonvanishing
margin is unavailable.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.WindowLadder

namespace RHTower

open Complex

/-- RH verified through the positive ordinate `T`, restricted to the open critical strip. -/
def RHVerifiedThrough (T : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃ρ : ℂ⦄, xi ρ = 0 → 0 < ρ.re → ρ.re < 1 → 0 < ρ.im → ρ.im ≤ T → ρ.re = 1 / 2

/-- **The verified-height interface has an unconditional base.**  At every nonpositive height there
is no positive-ordinate zero to check, so `RHVerifiedThrough T` holds vacuously.  In particular this
discharges the initial-height hypothesis of the amplification theorems at `T = 0`; only their new
zero census remains. -/
theorem rhVerifiedThrough_of_nonpos {T : ℝ} (hT : T ≤ 0) : RHVerifiedThrough T := by
  intro ρ _ _ _ him0 himT
  exfalso
  linarith

theorem rhVerifiedThrough_zero : RHVerifiedThrough 0 :=
  rhVerifiedThrough_of_nonpos le_rfl

/-- Strip zeros in the half-open height increment `(H, U]`. -/
def stripZeroIncrement (H U : ℝ) : Set ℂ :=
  {ρ : ℂ | 0 < ρ.re ∧ ρ.re < 1 ∧ 0 < ρ.im ∧ H < ρ.im ∧ ρ.im ≤ U ∧ xi ρ = 0}

/-- Every bounded height increment contains finitely many strip zeros. -/
theorem stripZeroIncrement_finite (H U : ℝ) : (stripZeroIncrement H U).Finite := by
  refine (stripZeros_finite (U + 1)).subset ?_
  rintro ρ ⟨hre0, hre1, him0, himH, himU, hzero⟩
  exact ⟨⟨hre0, hre1, him0.le, lt_of_le_of_lt himU (lt_add_one U)⟩, hzero⟩

/-- The height increment is closed under critical-line reflection. -/
theorem lineReflect_mem_stripZeroIncrement {H U : ℝ} {ρ : ℂ}
    (hρ : ρ ∈ stripZeroIncrement H U) : lineReflect ρ ∈ stripZeroIncrement H U := by
  obtain ⟨hre0, hre1, him0, himH, himU, hzero⟩ := hρ
  have him : (lineReflect ρ).im = ρ.im := by simp [lineReflect]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [lineReflect_re]; linarith
  · rw [lineReflect_re]; linarith
  · rw [him]; exact him0
  · rw [him]; exact himH
  · rw [him]; exact himU
  · simp only [lineReflect]
    rw [xi_one_sub, xi_conj, hzero, map_zero]

/-- **A one-new-zero census amplifies a verified RH height.**  If RH is verified through `H` and
